title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 2 opens with the title 'Families of classes of cycles modulo Albanese equivalence'. It continues §1 (previous page), where Albanese equivalence on A^i(X) was defined through parameter varieties. A cycle Z on X×T and a 0-cycle n on T of degree 0 with S_T(n)=0 give a cycle Z(n) that is declared equivalent to 0. Here S_T is the Albanese summation map.

Theorem 2.1, in modern terms:
- Setup: X^n and Y^m are smooth projective, and Z ∈ A^i_alb(X×Y) is a correspondence. Z acts on 0-cycles of Y by v ↦ Z(v) = pr_{X*}(Z · pr_Y^* v). By definition of the equivalence, this descends to a map A_{0,alb}(Y) → A^i_alb(X).
- Identification: zero-cycles modulo Albanese equivalence form the graded group A*_Y(k) = ⊔_n A^{(n)}_Y(k). The degree-n piece A^{(n)}_Y is the Albanese torsor, and the identification is given by the summation map S_Y. So Z yields a group homomorphism u*_Z : A*_Y(k) → A^i_alb(X), characterised by Z(v) = u_Z(S(v)) for all v, or for v of fixed degree n if one restricts to A^{(n)}.
- Degree-0 part: the restriction is u_Z : A_Y(k) = A^0_Y(k) → A^i_alb(X), from the Albanese variety itself.
  - (i) u_Z depends only on the class of Z in a coarser group A^{i,τ}(X×Y). This is marked 'to be reserved for later'. Pullbacks pr_X^*W act by deg(v)·W and so die on degree 0, which is consistent.
  - (ii) u_Z is algebraic up to isogeny. There is an isogeny of abelian varieties φ : A' → A_Y and a cycle Z' on X×A' with Z'(0)=0. With this normalisation, a' ↦ Z'(a') is automatically a homomorphism modulo Albanese equivalence, because the 0-cycle (a+b)−(a)−(b)+(0) has S=0. The claim is u_Z∘φ(k) = v_{Z'}.
- Proof, on the next page: choose a family of 0-cycles U on Y×A_Y with S_Y(U(a)) = a. Such a family exists only after an isogeny, e.g. via a curve C ⊂ Y with J(C) → Alb(Y) surjective. Then set Z'(a) := Z(U(a)), which is the composite correspondence Z∘U.

Purpose: show that the image in codimension-i cycles of the Albanese part of 0-cycles under any correspondence is 'regularly' parametrised by an abelian variety. This is a step toward representability of algebraically trivial cycles modulo this equivalence, within the programme on cycles and the standard and Hodge conjectures.
errors: The identification A_{0,alb}(Y) ≅ A*_Y(k) assumes k is algebraically closed, or at least that Y has rational points or 0-cycles of degree 1 in each degree. Over a general field the degree-n torsors may have no k-points.

The section U with S_Y(U(a)) = a generally exists only after an isogeny; this is why φ is needed. The page states this correctly. The next page's proof is still incomplete ('Mais on ne sait pas si on peut...').
Notational drift: this page writes Z' ∈ A^i_alb(X × A'), while the next page writes A^i_alg(X' × A'). The intended group is presumably A^i_alb(X×A').

Point (i), dependence only on the class in A^{i,τ}(X×Y), is asserted without proof and explicitly deferred. The meaning of τ, presumably a coarser numerical-type equivalence, is not defined on this page.

ideas.what: Definition of an 'Albanese equivalence' on cycles of arbitrary codimension: the equivalence generated by images Z(n) of Albanese-trivial degree-0 zero-cycles n on parameter varieties T under correspondences Z on X×T.
ideas.modern_name: Saito filtration / subgroup F^2_S generated by correspondence images of Albanese kernels T(Y); quotient CH^i/F^2_S
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Saito, 'Abelian varieties attached to cycles of intermediate dimension' (Nagoya Math. J., 1979); later Murre (algebraic representatives, 1983–85) and the Bloch–Beilinson filtration literature
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA/FGA as far as known; unsure about letters

ideas.what: Zero-cycles modulo Albanese equivalence identified with k-points of the graded Albanese A*_Y = ⊔ A^{(n)}_Y (Albanese torsors) via the summation map S_Y.
ideas.modern_name: Albanese map on CH_0 / Albanese torsors Alb^n_Y
ideas.where_published: Related material in FGA (Picard scheme); torsor formulation unsure

ideas.what: A correspondence Z induces a homomorphism u_Z from Alb_Y(k) to codim-i cycles mod Albanese equivalence. Up to isogeny it is induced by a cycle on X×A' normalised by Z'(0)=0, obtained by composing with a family U of 0-cycles with S_Y(U(a)) = a.
ideas.modern_name: Regular homomorphisms / action of correspondences on Albanese; algebraically parametrised families of cycles (Samuel, Murre)

ideas.what: Normalisation trick: a family Z' over an abelian variety with Z'(0)=0 is automatically a homomorphism modulo Albanese equivalence, since (a+b)−(a)−(b)+(0) is Albanese-trivial.
ideas.modern_name: Theorem of the cube / additivity of families over abelian varieties modulo Albanese kernel

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines, c. 1965–71, an 'Albanese equivalence' on cycles of all codimensions: correspondence images of Albanese-trivial 0-cycles. He sets up the functoriality of correspondences and the abelian-variety factorisation of the induced maps. This anticipates H. Saito's 1979 subgroup generated by images of Albanese kernels and its use for abelian varieties attached to intermediate cycles. Together with Thm 1.6 on the previous page (alg. trivial · alg. trivial = 0 mod this equivalence), it amounts to an early study of the 'F^2' step of a Bloch–Beilinson-type filtration.
missed.quote: Familles de classes de cycles mod équiv. d'Alb. ... Z ∈ A^i_alb(X × Y), d'où une application v ↦ Z(v) de A_{0 alb}(Y) ... dans A^i_alb(X)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is historical priority evidence: Grothendieck considered the Albanese-kernel-generated filtration, now attributed to Saito, Murre and Bloch–Beilinson, about a decade earlier. Combined with the deferred point (i), it hints that he wanted representability of A^i_{alb,0}(X) by an abelian variety. That question is still only partially settled (algebraic representatives; Saito's question).

missed.claim: Point (i) is left open and explicitly deferred: the induced map on the Albanese depends only on Z modulo a coarser τ-type equivalence on X×Y.
missed.quote: (i) Il ne dépend que de la classe de Z dans A^{i,τ}(X × Y) [A réserver pour plus tard]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a statement of the kind 'the action of correspondences on Albanese/Saito graded pieces factors through numerical or homological equivalence'. It relates to conjectures (Bloch–Beilinson, Murre) about filtrations on Chow groups, which remain open in general.

deep.surprise_reason: The individual tools are classical: the Albanese action of correspondences and regular homomorphisms. However, systematically defining Albanese equivalence in all codimensions and studying its functoriality anticipates H. Saito (1979) and the F^2 part of Bloch–Beilinson filtrations. This seems not to be credited to Grothendieck. Moderate historical interest rather than a new theorem.
transcription_corrections: 'pour tout v de degré —, si on regarde la restriction en degré —': the dashes stand for a degree index, almost surely 'n', matching the struck-out A^{(n)}_Y(k).
'de VA' (isogénie de VA = variétés abéliennes); the image shows 'UA' written above, i.e. 'VA'.
The small circled annotation under A*_Y(k) reads like 'Alb', a note that A*_Y means the graded Albanese (Alb*_Y), not an extra factor.
Line 3 overlay reads 'A_{0 alb}(Y) ≃ Alb*_Y(k), dans A^i_alb(X)', and the boxed alternative reads 'si A_{0 alb}(Y) ≃^{S_Y} A*_Y(k)'; the transcription is essentially right.
The last line reads 'Z' ∈ A^i_alb(' with X×A' cut off at the page edge, continued on the next page.
